old: Chemical compounds are described in many ways, including molecular formulas, chemical structures, generic, systematic, common, and trade names. Governmental agencies rely on CAS Registry Numbers for substance identification in regulatory applications because they are unique, easily validated, and internationally recognised. CAS RNs are used by the Chemical Abstracts Service Registry. A CAS Registry Number is a numeric identifier that can contain up to 10 digits, divided by hyphens into three parts. The right-most digit is a check digit used to verify the validity and uniqueness of the entire number.

old: An MDL Molfile is a file format for holding information about the atoms, bonds, connectivity and coordinates of a molecule. The molfile consists of some header information, the Connection Table (CT) containing atom info, then bond connections and types, followed by sections for more complex information. The molfile is sufficiently common that most, if not all, cheminformatics software systems/applications are able to read the format, though not always to the same degree. It is also supported by some computational software such as Mathematica. The current de facto standard version is molfile V2000, although, more recently, the V3000 format has been circulating widely enough to present a potential compatibility issue for those applications that are not yet V3000-capable. Please note that this format is only available after registration on the Dassault Systems website.
new: A plain-text chemical file format from the CTfile family first published by MDL. It stores a molecule's atoms, bonds and coordinates as a connection table with optional property blocks (V2000 and V3000). Almost all cheminformatics software reads it, so it is a standard way to exchange structures, for example as input to QSAR and read-across tools.

Toxin and Toxin Target Database (T3DB)The Toxin and Toxin Target Database (T3DB) is a bioinformatics resource that combines detailed toxin data with comprehensive toxin target information. Each toxin record (ToxCard) contains over 90 data fields and holds information such as chemical properties and descriptors, toxicity values, molecular and cellular interactions, and medical information. The Data Stewardship Wizard is an open-source web platform for writing data management plans together, developed within ELIXIR and begun at the Czech Technical University in Prague. Data stewards encode guidance as knowledge models that drive adaptive questionnaires, and the answers are exported through document templates as readable or machine-actionable plans. Organisations can run their own instances, and the FIP Wizard is built on it.

A registry that mints global, unique identifiers (ERM followed by eight digits) for nanomaterials and other materials studied in research projects, including materials whose composition is not disclosed and specific batches or variants. Projects reserve an identifier when they plan to study a material, so that internal documents, datasets and publications refer to the same material and can later be linked to its public data; the identifiers resolve through identifiers.org.

The Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO) is an application ontology from EMBL-EBI for the experimental variables recorded in EBI databases, such as diseases, phenotypes, anatomy, cell types and cell lines, chemical compounds and assays. It brings together classes from reference ontologies such as Uberon, ChEBI, the Cell Ontology and MONDO and links them, so that resources such as Expression Atlas, BioSamples, the GWAS Catalog and Open Targets can annotate samples and studies consistently and integrate their data.

The PubChem Compound Identifier (CID) is the integer accession that NCBI's PubChem gives to each unique chemical structure, obtained by standardising the structures in depositors' substance records. Registered at identifiers.org under the prefix pubchem.compound, a CID can be cited as a compact identifier that resolves to the compound's PubChem record, so data and metadata can refer to a chemical unambiguously.

TeSS (Training eSupport System) is ELIXIR's online registry of life-science training. It collects descriptions of training events and materials from ELIXIR Nodes and other providers, automatically (for example by harvesting Bioschemas markup) or by manual registration, and makes them searchable through a portal, an API and embeddable widgets.

Zenodo is a general-purpose open repository, built and run by CERN with OpenAIRE, where researchers from any discipline deposit datasets, software, publications and other research outputs. Each upload gets a DataCite DOI so it can be cited. GitHub repositories can be archived automatically, and records can be grouped in communities and linked to funder grants.
